title: Is the peak too late to vaccinate?
hook: The epidemic has peaked. Does protecting people now still change the ending?

knows: the SIR picture: susceptible, sick, recovered
an unchecked epidemic peaks and then declines
doesNotKnow: that at the peak many people have still never been infected
that protecting people at the peak still removes much of the remaining spread

misconception: Vaccinating after the peak (or at it) is pointless.
objective: The learner can explain that the peak is the middle of an epidemic: about a third of the town is still uninfected, so in this toy model vaccinating 20% of the town from those people at the peak keeps about 78% of the benefit of vaccinating on day 0.

claims.text: In the stage's toy SIR model (R0 = 3, 0.1% sick on day 0), with no vaccination 94% are eventually infected and new cases peak on day 19.
claims.source: Deterministic SIR, Euler step 0.01 day to day 200 (infection 0.6/day, recovery 0.2/day), replicated in artifacts/scratch/w3life/vacc.mjs: ever infected 0.9407, peak at day 19.19. No random seed.

claims.text: Vaccinating 20% of the town at once, all people not yet infected, brings the final infected share to 70% on day 0 and 76% at the peak (day 19): the peak saves 18.4 of the 23.8 points that day 0 saves, 77.5% of the benefit (shown as 78%). On day 40 the final share is 94%.
claims.source: artifacts/scratch/w3life/vacc.mjs (mode 'sus'): day 0 0.7031, day 19 0.7566, day 40 0.9359, none 0.9407; fraction 0.775. The brief's check (50%, 56%, 87%) did not reproduce in this model; see company/reviews/vaccinate-at-the-peak/build.md.

claims.text: On day 19, the peak, about 35% of the town has never been infected; the peak comes when the susceptible share falls to 1/R0.
claims.source: dI/dt = (beta S - gamma) I = 0 at S = 1/3 (peak at day 19.19); S at day 19 = 0.3455 in the same run. DISPUTED 2026-10-13: Numbers right (S at day 19 = 34.5%; peak at S=1/R0) but the reveal says 'most infections were still to come' at the peak. node: at day 19, 65.5% of the town has already been infected; only 28.6 points remain, 30% of the eventual 94%. So most infections have already happened. Fix: 'about a third of the town had never been infected' or 'nearly a third of the town was still to be infected', and drop 'most' and 'the middle of the epidemic'. | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Was '... so most of the epidemic's remaining infections are still to come' (disputed: 65.5% of the town has already been infected by day 19). Dropped 'most infections still to come' and 'the middle of the epidemic' from the reveal.

claims.text: If the 20% of doses went to random people (some already infected or recovered) instead of only to people not yet infected, vaccinating at the peak would keep only about 29% of the day-0 benefit.
claims.source: artifacts/scratch/w3life/vacc.mjs (mode 'random', doses = 0.2 x S): day 0 0.7034, day 19 0.8727, fraction 0.286. Disclosed in the reveal because the lesson's headline depends on the targeting assumption.

claims.text: The model is a made-up disease with random mixing, instant and perfect protection, and doses only to people not yet infected; it is a model result, not guidance.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question, on the stage ('Toy: ... all not yet infected') and in the reveal.

recall.question: In a simple well-mixed epidemic model with no interventions, roughly where is the epidemic when new cases peak?
options: Nearly over: almost everyone has been infected
Around the middle: many people have never been infected and many infections are still to come
Just starting: almost nobody has been infected
recall.why: The peak comes when the susceptible share falls to 1/R0; with R0 = 3 a third of people are still uninfected, so protecting them still changes the ending.
